t.1.91.1: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: There was a king, a lord of the earth, born of the lineage of Ikṣvāku, renowned as Mahābhiṣa, truthful in speech and true in valor.
t.1.91.2: With a thousand Aśvamedha sacrifices and a hundred Vājapeya sacrifices he pleased the lord of the gods, and thereby that mighty lord attained heaven.
t.1.91.3: Then, once upon a time, the gods were attending upon Brahmā. Royal seers were present there, and so was that king Mahābhiṣa.
t.1.91.4: Then Gaṅgā, best of rivers, approached the Grandfather; her garment, bright as the moon, was blown up by the wind.
t.1.91.5: Then the hosts of gods at once turned their faces downward; but the royal seer Mahābhiṣa, unabashed, gazed at the river.
t.1.91.6: That Mahābhiṣa was cursed by the blessed Brahmā and told: "Having been born among mortals, you will regain the worlds once more."
t.1.91.7: Having considered all the kings rich in austerity, that king chose Pratīpa, a man of great splendor, to be his father.
t.1.91.9: But she, as she went along the path, saw the Vasus, the gods who dwell in heaven, their bodies shattered and their vigor struck down by dejection.
t.1.91.8: The river, having seen that King Mahābhiṣa fallen from his composure, went back, that best of rivers, dwelling on him alone in her mind.
t.1.91.11: The gods, the Vasus, said to her: "O great river, we have indeed been cursed in anger by the great-souled Vasiṣṭha for a small offense."
t.1.91.10: Seeing them in that state, the best of rivers asked them: "What is this? Why have you lost your proper form? Is all well with the dwellers of heaven?"
t.1.91.13: Out of anger he cursed us, saying, "Be born in a womb!" What has been spoken by that expounder of the Veda cannot be made otherwise.
t.1.91.12: For all of us, bewildered, once trespassed upon that best of seers, Vasiṣṭha, as he sat hidden at the twilight juncture.
t.1.91.14: Therefore, becoming a mortal woman yourself, give birth to us Vasus as your sons on earth; we would not enter the impure womb of mortal women.
t.1.91.15: Thus addressed, Gaṅgā said "So be it" to those Vasus, and then spoke these words: "Among mortals, which best of men will be your begetter?"
t.1.91.16: The son of Pratīpa, a righteous king named Śaṃtanu, will come to be in the world of men; he shall be our begetter.
t.1.91.18: You should cast your own sons into the waters as soon as they are born, so that our release may come before long, O you who move through the three worlds.
t.1.91.19: Gaṅgā said: "So I shall do this; let a son be granted to him. His union with me, undertaken for the sake of a son, shall not be fruitless."
t.1.91.17: Gaṅgā said: This is my view as well, O gods, just as you have told me, O sinless ones. I shall do what is dear to him, and this is also what you desire.
t.1.91.21: But his lineage will not continue among mortals; therefore that son of yours, though mighty, will be without a son.
t.1.91.20: Each one of us will give an eighth part of his vigor; by that vigor a son will be born to you, the son he desires.
t.1.91.22: Having thus made a compact with Gaṅgā, the Vasus, their minds delighted, went straightway wherever they wished.
